record_type_quote:
In our study, we determined whether we could replicate the results
of the IMSGC and whether more SNPs are genome-wide significantly associated with MS. We assessed the association between
the 17 IMSGC SNPs and MS in three cohorts (total number of subjects 3981, among these 1853 cases).

targets.authors: Hafler, D. A., Compston, A., Sawcer, S., Lander, E. S., Daly, M. J., De Jager, P. L. et al.
targets.title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study.

targets.outcome_quote:
Bold entries signifies SNPs achieving genome-wide significance (Po5E–8) in meta-analysis. Italic: SNPs for which contradicting results were obtained between the original report of IMSGC and our
       data, as indicated by at least 10 increase in the P-value.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper re-tests the 17 IMSGC associations in new Dutch and Canadian samples. It confirms several associations but explicitly calls three of the original associations false positives. The conclusion confirms named genes rather than giving an overall verdict that all 17 findings replicated. Rubio et al. supplies earlier replication results for pooling, rather than being the finding explicitly re-tested.

reasoning: Completed new-sample replication of the IMSGC genomewide study (reference 2). The meta-analysis incorporates earlier results but does not change the new-sample replication relationship.
